title: [C14T3] - Hydroelectricity generation
prompt: The diagram below shows how electricity is generated in a hydroelectric power station. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagram illustrates the process of generating electricity in a hydroelectric power station.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the electricity generation process involves multiple stages that operate differently during day and night cycles. The process begins with water stored in a high-level reservoir and ends with electricity being distributed to the national grid.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: During daytime operations, water flows from the high-level reservoir through the dam to the power station below. The intake system, which remains open during the day, allows water to flow downward and operate the reversible turbines. These turbines drive the generator to produce electricity, which is then transmitted through power lines to the national grid. Simultaneously, excess water continues flowing to a low-level reservoir located at the bottom of the system.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: At night, the process reverses to store energy for future use. The intake closes, and the reversible turbines switch to pumping mode, powered by electricity from the grid. Water is pumped from the low-level reservoir back up to the high-level reservoir, effectively recharging the system. This pumped-storage mechanism ensures continuous electricity supply by storing energy during low-demand periods and releasing it when needed during peak hours.
